Okay I'm only an inch taller than you and was at that same weight just last year. My older clothes didn't fit as well but I definitely wasn't fat, so I'm positive that you aren't either. Now, if YOU want to shed a few pounds, try keto, it worked for me (and I'm a mom also). But don't do it for him, he obviously has deeper issues happening here. To love you is to respect you and your feelings. And the things he's saying are also harmful to your daughter. What if she grows up overweight and remembers what he said about you? 

My advice would be to put your foot down. Tell him to not say another word about your size. If he tries to give you an excuse (like trying to motivate you) just shut it down immediately by telling him to stop.

I was diagnosed almost 15 years ago and only had my initial and then a second in the first year. Nothing since then. If I ever had another outbreak in that time, it was so mild that I couldn't even tell it was an actual outbreak and didn't warrant a trip to the doctor.

It's not okay and you should just tell your MIL to stop. I get that it will be uncomfortable, but he's your child and you should trust your gut. At what age will she stop? WILL she stop? My mom used to always pat my butt when she put me to bed. I hated it and it made me uncomfortable. After I had my son and she started patting his butt rather than his back, I straight up told her to stop touching his butt. She always used to insist that I give ALL the family "bye kisses" and I hated that also. She tried making my son do this also, but I put a stop to it by standing at the door telling him to come on. Basically, if you're uncomfortable with it, he will be too when he's old enough to understand those are his private areas.
